answers.decision: Small software teams using AI coding assistants struggle with inconsistent code, unclear requirements, regressions, and conflicting changes. We want a guided governance toolkit that helps founders and developers plan, review, test, and release software with clear ownership and approval gates.

Founder/product owner: define goals, prioritize MVP features, clarify requirements, approve scope. Developer: read approved tasks, implement changes, run tests, submit PRs. Reviewer/module owner: approve task readiness, review changes, verify evidence, protect module boundaries. Technical Owner: approve architecture, define quality targets, resolve conflicts, oversee safeguards. Release Approver/operations owner: assess release readiness, approve releases, monitor service health, coordinate rollback.

Within 30 days, all active developers use the approved task workflow and PR checklist. Within 60 days, every PR runs governance checks and application tests, with required human reviews before merging. Within 90 days, reduce regression defects found after merging by 30% compared with the first 30-day baseline.
A - Responsive web only

MVP 1 needs guided project discovery with save/resume, requirements and feature tracking, seven-block task templates, architecture checks, PR metadata validation, human approval records, verification reports, and installation guidance. Git integration supplies changed-file evidence; GitHub integration provides CI checks and branch protection after authorized setup. No payments, email/SMS, external identity provider, or production deployment automation is required for MVP 1.

FEAT-001 guided project discovery with save/resume; FEAT-002 requirements, MVP scope, and feature register validation; FEAT-003 seven-block task templates and approval metadata checks; FEAT-004 architecture boundary checks; FEAT-005 PR validation using actual changed files and verification evidence; FEAT-006 local verification and GitHub CI configuration; FEAT-007 branch-protection setup and verification guidance.

MVP 1 non-goals: web dashboard, mobile app, payments, email/SMS notifications, external identity integration, automatic human approvals, live repository changes without authorization, and production deployment automation. MVP 2 candidates: a read-only governance dashboard, traceability reports linking requirements to PRs and test results, and adapters for additional repository platforms. Candidates remain unapproved until assessed and prioritized.
